stories.title: Air India, AI Express To Operate As 'One Group, Two Brands': Here's What That Means - NDTV
Air India group targets synergy to cut losses
stories.summary: Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam will implement a One AI Group approach to integrate its full-service and budget arms. The move aims to address operational challenges and curb losses that have reached Rs 60,000 crore since Tata took control in 2022. The airlines will remain legally distinct.

stories.title: Navi Mumbai Airport Crosses 4 Million Passengers Milestone Ahead Of First Anniversary - NDTV
IndiGo aircraft returns to service after 62-day grounding
stories.summary: An IndiGo Airbus A321-251 NX has resumed operations after being grounded for 62 days following a hard landing at Delhi airport. The aircraft underwent landing gear replacement and mandatory checks before departing for Nagpur. It spent two months in a hangar waiting for its turn.

stories.title: Cabinet approves container terminal and Assam airport
stories.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a Rs 4,288.26 crore container terminal at Kamarajar Port and a Rs 2,014 crore greenfield airport at Doloo. The projects are intended to expand capacity in Tamil Nadu and Assam. Infrastructure projects are now moving from approval to construction.

stories.title: New Rs 2,014-crore airport approved for Silchar
stories.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a greenfield airport at Doloo to replace the existing civil enclave at Silchar Airport. The Airports Authority of India will manage the project, which aims to bypass the space and operational limits of the current defence-landlocked site.

stories.title: Cabinet clears Rs 1,677 crore civil enclave project at Srinagar airport - DD News
Government approves Rs 2,014-crore greenfield airport in Assam
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a new greenfield airport at Doloo in Assam to replace the constrained Silchar civil enclave. The project will feature a 12,351-square-metre terminal with an annual capacity of 1.01 million passengers. The current airport is located on defence land with limited room for growth.

stories.title: IndiGo adds Bhavnagar to network with Navi Mumbai flights
stories.summary: IndiGo will launch 14 weekly direct flights between Bhavnagar and Navi Mumbai starting 29 March 2026. The route will be served by ATR aircraft, making Bhavnagar the airline's 97th domestic destination. The city is a commercial hub for manufacturing, shipbreaking, salt production, and the diamond trade.

stories.title: EasyJet airline business records £195m loss
stories.summary: EasyJet reported a £195m headline pretax loss for its airline business in the year ending September 30, 2026. The group remained profitable overall due to its holidays division, which earned £266m. Flying people is currently less lucrative than booking their vacations.

stories.title: Norse Atlantic faces liquidity crisis and lease cancellation
stories.summary: Norse Atlantic Airways described its financial situation as critical, citing a need for short-term financing. Following the announcement, Pakistan International Airlines cancelled its wet lease of the carrier's B787-9 aircraft. The airline is currently engaged in discussions with parties regarding its future.

stories.title: American Airlines struggles to match rival fare premiums
stories.summary: American Airlines is trailing the financial performance of Delta and United, according to Seaport Research Partners. Analyst Dan McKenzie estimates American needs $4.5 billion in additional annual revenue to match its competitors, who successfully command higher fares from passengers. Demand is apparently not the only factor.

stories.title: Fly Alliance suspends operations for restructuring
stories.summary: Private flight provider Fly Alliance suspended operations on Monday to begin a business restructuring. Members may transfer prepaid credits to FlyExclusive under a management services agreement. CEO Christopher Tasca stated that members can keep their outstanding balances with his company during the process.

stories.title: JetBlue reduces international footprint
stories.summary: JetBlue has ended 11 international routes as part of a broader reduction in its overseas service. International departures fell 9 percent compared to last November, with the carrier's international share dropping from 23 percent to 20 percent. The airline remains the fourth-largest US operator for international service.

stories.title: Delta plans international expansion for 2027
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines plans to increase its international departures by 6 percent for the third quarter of 2027 compared to 2026. The carrier expects to operate 258 daily international departures, including 15 new or returning routes. Plans remain subject to change as the airline firms up its schedule.

stories.title: United Airlines sees low load factors on Greenland route
stories.summary: United Airlines' nonstop service between Newark and Nuuk is operating with more than half of its seats empty. Despite the opening of a new international airport in Nuuk, the route has struggled with high costs and limited tourism infrastructure. The link is currently a quiet one.

stories.title: IndiGo suspends Manchester route due to rising costs
stories.summary: IndiGo will suspend flights to Manchester on 31 August 2026, citing airspace restrictions and high operating costs. The airline plans to return one of its leased Boeing 787-9 aircraft as a result. The route was deemed commercially unsustainable under current conditions.

stories.title: Air India expands Canada capacity for winter season
stories.summary: Air India will launch a three-times-weekly non-stop service between Mumbai and Toronto for the 2026-27 winter season. The airline is also deploying Boeing 787-9 aircraft on its Delhi-Toronto route, increasing total capacity by 4,400 seats per month. Premium seating capacity is expected to rise by 71 percent.

stories.title: Malaysia Aviation Group orders 10 Boeing 787s
stories.summary: Malaysia Aviation Group has signed a firm order for 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, with options for six more, to modernize its fleet. The aircraft are scheduled for delivery between 2032 and 2035. The airline currently operates an Airbus fleet, and these will be its first Boeing widebody jets.

stories.title: Malaysia Airlines to become first 787 operator in country
stories.summary: Malaysia Aviation Group has ordered 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, with options for six more, to replace its long-haul fleet. The aircraft will be delivered between 2032 and 2035. The airline says the acquisition is a strategic investment in its future. Financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed.

stories.title: K2 Aviation acquires six Boeing 737-800s
stories.summary: Dublin-based lessor K2 Aviation has agreed to purchase six Boeing 737-800s from SMBC Aviation Capital. The aircraft are currently in service with six different airline customers. The transaction follows a portfolio purchase K2 Aviation completed with Carlyle Aviation Partners in September.

stories.title: GE Aerospace Lands First GEnx Engine Deal with Malaysia Aviation Group as Regional Demand Grows - Benzinga
US proposes 10 percent tariff on Brazilian aircraft
stories.summary: The United States has proposed a 10 percent tariff on finished aircraft imported from Brazil, potentially impacting Embraer. The proposal aims to end an exemption granted in July 2026. Finished aircraft are currently Brazil's fourth-largest export to the United States, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative.

stories.title: Bombardier says labor costs are outpacing pricing
stories.summary: Bombardier service centers are facing margin pressure as the cost to provide an hour of technician labor now exceeds the rate charged to customers. The disclosure highlights similar challenges facing both original equipment manufacturers and independent maintenance providers in the current market for aircraft services.

stories.title: Turkish aeroengine maker to build Bulgarian facility
stories.summary: Tusas Engine Industries plans to invest $90 million to establish an engine component manufacturing hub in Plovdiv, Bulgaria. The project is expected to create 170 jobs and marks the company's first manufacturing footprint within the European Union. Plovdiv was selected over two other European locations.

stories.title: Northern Jet opens MRO subsidiary in Orlando
stories.summary: Northern Jet has launched a Part 145 maintenance subsidiary, Northern Air, based at Orlando Executive Airport. The new 35,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to open in January. The company plans to hire additional technicians to support its expansion into the business aviation maintenance market in the Southeast.

stories.title: Vietjet and Haite Group partner on technical support
stories.summary: Vietjet and Haite Group have signed a memorandum of understanding to cooperate on aviation industrial and technical services. The partnership covers aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul, as well as technical workforce training. The parties are also exploring new aviation industrial capabilities at Long Thanh International Airport.

stories.title: FAA links ground stop to network configuration error
stories.summary: A nationwide US air traffic ground stop on November 13 was caused by a single configuration error during routine maintenance by a contractor. Laboratory tests confirmed the failure occurred while upgrading network equipment in Arkansas. The agency is now reviewing how it oversees contractor work on critical infrastructure.

stories.title: FAA chief to testify before Congress following nationwide ground stop - upi
FAA chief to testify on air traffic control overhaul in wake of outages - The Hill
FAA administrator requests $50 billion for system upgrades
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and President Donald Trump are calling for $50 billion in additional funding for the FAA following a recent nationwide ground stop. The request represents a significant increase from the $10 billion the agency sought earlier this year. Congress is currently in a lame-duck session.

stories.title: FAA mandates tower supervision for runway operations
stories.summary: The FAA now requires dedicated tower watch supervision for all line up and wait operations. The rule, which became effective November 24, makes a previously recommended supervisory arrangement mandatory. Controllers have expressed concern that the new staffing requirement could lead to flight delays during the holiday travel period.

stories.title: Amazon drone crashes in Michigan
stories.summary: An Amazon Prime Air MK30 drone crashed onto a garage in Huntington Woods, Michigan, on November 20 after delivering a package. No injuries were reported. The FAA has confirmed it is investigating the incident, which occurred in a residential neighborhood after the drone became tangled in power lines.

stories.title: Amazon drone crash prompts FAA investigation
stories.summary: An Amazon MK30 drone struck a fiber-optic cable and tangled in power lines before crashing onto a garage in Michigan on November 20. The FAA has opened an investigation into the incident. This is the latest in a series of reported Amazon Prime Air delivery mishaps.

stories.title: Mississippi plane crash highlights insurance gaps
stories.summary: Six people died when a Cessna 210 crashed into the Gulf of Mexico on Tuesday. The incident has drawn attention to the fact that standard travel insurance policies often do not cover passengers on private or non-commercial flights. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

stories.title: ANA establishes pilot training subsidiary in Japan
stories.summary: ANA Holdings has established ANA Next Aviation to provide ab initio training for future commercial airline pilots in Japan. The company says the move addresses a potential shortage of flight crews. The venture is a collaboration with Japan, as the country prepares for future staffing needs.

stories.title: AAIB seeks minimum flying experience for flight instructors
stories.summary: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau has asked the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to mandate minimum flying experience for new commercial pilot licence holders working as instructors. The recommendation follows a fatal 2023 crash involving a trainer aircraft. Accident rates at flying training organisations have reportedly increased.

stories.title: AAIB report links trainer crashes to training and SOP failures
stories.summary: An AAIB analysis of trainer aircraft crashes from 2015 to 2025 attributes most incidents to inadequate training, poor supervision, and violations of standard operating procedures. The report notes that commercial pilots are often moved into instructional roles quickly. Safety culture remains a primary concern for investigators.

stories.title: China integrates combat drones into pilot training
stories.summary: The People's Liberation Army is using manned-unmanned teaming exercises to test pilots against complex battlefield conditions. An aviation brigade under the Southern Theatre Command has incorporated these simulations into ground-based flight training. The system aims to prepare pilots for scenarios involving electromagnetic interference and waves of targets.

stories.title: China embeds ‘loyal wingman’ drone simulations in fighter pilot training - South China Morning Post
Dayalans Aviation targets 2027 launch for new flight academy
stories.summary: Dayalans Aviation has received approval from the Airports Authority of India to establish a flying training organisation at Hubballi Airport. The company expects to begin operations by April or May 2027. The academy will be the second flight training provider at the site once infrastructure development is complete.

stories.title: Nigeria supports Baze University pilot training facility
stories.summary: Baze Aviation School is developing a flight training facility in Abuja with federal government support. Minister of Aviation Festus Keyamo endorsed the project as a regional training center. The school aims to reduce reliance on overseas training, with runway sub-base construction currently at 95 percent completion.

stories.title: TAAG Angola Airlines opens flight simulator facility
stories.summary: TAAG Angola Airlines has inaugurated a new flight simulator facility in Luanda featuring Boeing 737 and single-engine simulators. The airline intends to use the center for preliminary trainee assessments. The Boeing 737 device is currently awaiting certification from the National Civil Aviation Authority before it can be used.

stories.title: Tassili Travail Aérien launches flight academy in Algeria
stories.summary: Tassili Travail Aérien has launched a flight academy at Sayada Airport with training scheduled to begin on 2 January 2027. The academy offers private, commercial, and airline transport pilot qualifications. Pre-registration is currently open for the first intake of students at the new domestic training facility.
